As the ideal entry into the HNL, in his words, the biggest Croatian derby between Dinamo and Hajduk imposes itself, played in a lineup the channel has not had in the studio for a long time.\n\nŠpehar then introduces himself and announces the guests: **Duje Granić**, **Luka Vujić** and **Marino Durdov**.      "content": "**Duje Granić** describes the match as two extremes. On one side, the atmosphere and the home side's comeback were strong and created a fun day for being at the stadium. On the other side, the rain was a serious problem in the media section: journalists had to work on laptops under umbrellas, even though the stadium was supposed to be covered.\n\nGranić recalls that the football at the end of the match was chaotic, comparing it to the famous Christmas truce between the English and the Germans during the First World War. He adds that he and his colleague from Ofenziva, Marko Štrkalj, agreed that the whole experience was fun, but that one must not ignore the fact that the pitch was not in good condition.\n\nGranić emphasises that the infrastructure problems at Poljud, which have been discussed for a long time, are unacceptable, especially because they repeat even after so many years. After the presentation of the new **Maksimir** project, a debate about Split also started, where fans and the club Hajduk increasingly demand a new stadium. Prime Minister **Andrej Plenković** announced a reconstruction, which further sparked public debate about the future of the stadium.\n\nThe presenter sets out a dual perspective: the match can be viewed as a 'vintage derby' that will be remembered for a long time, but also as a poor picture of Croatian league football, which once again showed the weaknesses of the infrastructure before domestic and foreign audiences.      "content": "**Luka Vujić** believes the downpour came at the ideal moment because it shows why the topic of a new stadium is current. He points out that this is the first heavy rain since the Ultra festival was in Split, and that the problems can be seen both in the stands and in the auxiliary rooms.\n\nVujić stresses that Split probably does not need two new stadiums, especially because Spaladium Arena is not commercially used enough. He also talks about the idea of giving the stadium a cosmetic makeover, for which he believes there is no point: a more thorough renovation or the construction of a new facility is needed, either at Poljud or somewhere else.\n\nVujić adds that the argument about Poljud's cultural heritage status is weak, since protection was granted only about ten years ago, mainly so that funds could be drawn from European funds. Dinamo could not get out of its own back line, and the middle of the pitch was congested. In such moments it is hard to talk about real tactics and set-up. Still, he stresses that Hajduk's greatest advantage was that the team gradually rose through the match, while Dinamo, after the goal, fell into a kind of decline.",

Through such examples he stresses that different perceptions of a match often come down to whether one looks at the result or at the tactical process.\n\nIn the key moments, in his opinion, Hajduk never showed signs of falling apart. He adds that the character of a side is best seen precisely in the defensive phase, when it shows how much the team is truly at its peak.",

     "content": "**Luka Vujić** follows on from the discussion and gives a clearer view on the distribution of centre-backs. He believes that Hajduk will probably go with a deeper defence in certain matches, and that the key lies in the profiles of players who can cover depth across a wide area.\n\nVujić points out that one of the centre-backs is the only one who can be relied on to cover depth, and that in defensive phases he is calmer and more reliable in positioning, although he is slower in reading the game.      "subtitle": "Bamba: an unpredictable winger who seeks continuity",
     "screenshot_description": "Presenter Renato Špehar and guests Duje Granić and Luka Vujić in the studio with a statistical overview of the derby, with emphasis on Bamba's performance (goal, dribbles, created chances).",
     "content": "The conversation about Hajduk's individual players moves on to **Bamba**, whom presenter **Renato Špehar** names player of the match. Špehar also recalls that **Duje Granić** after the match with Milin expressed regret that he would no longer like to see him at Hajduk, and now, as he points out, his performance is phenomenal. In his words, the question is one of usage: Bamba is a player who lives off continuity and plays best when he regularly gets minutes, while longer periods on the bench make it hard for him to find his rhythm again. Vujić notes that coach Garcia has given him a regular place in the last nine rounds, which suits him. He especially highlights his speed and his ability to attack empty space behind the last line, so he handled the long ball in the derby excellently. According to Vujić's assessment, Bamba could be one of the key triggers for going forward in European matches, including the clash with Ajax. Still, he stresses that Garcia succeeded in instilling confidence in Bamba, and Granić himself says that this player could become Hajduk's best winger if he manages to balance energy, decision-making and focus. Granić further points to missed chances in situations where he could have decided differently, such as passing to Šega or choosing between a shot and a return pass.
